content.text: 🤿 Verbs
🔁 Review

In our previous lesson, we explored the structure and formation of sentences in English. We discussed how sentences are organized with subjects, predicates, and various complements to convey meaning effectively.
Quick Practice:
Identify the subject and predicate in this sentence: "The experienced teacher carefully explained the complex grammar rules."
Transform this simple sentence into a compound sentence: "She arrived late."
Create one complex sentence using a subordinate clause.
🎯 Overview
Verbs are words that express actions, occurrences, or states of being. They are the core of any sentence, showing what the subject is doing, experiencing, or being.

English verbs can be categorized in several ways: action verbs (run, eat, write), linking verbs (be, seem, become), auxiliary verbs (have, do, will), and modal verbs (can, should, might). Each type serves different functions in expressing meaning, time, and relationships.

We use verbs to indicate when something happens (tense), how it happens (aspect), who performs the action (voice), and the speaker's attitude toward the action (mood). Understanding verbs is crucial because they drive the meaning of sentences and determine how other elements function.
🏊 Can you do?
Fill in the blanks with the appropriate form of the verbs in parentheses:

a. She _______ (work) for this company since 2015. b. By the time we arrived, they _______ (leave) already. c. I _______ (think) about changing my career path lately. d. If I _______ (know) about the problem earlier, I would have fixed it.
Choose the correct verb form:

a. The team has/have won three matches this season. b. Neither the students nor the teacher was/were prepared for the surprise quiz. c. Each of the participants is/are required to submit their forms. d. A number of issues has/have been raised during the meeting.
Rewrite these sentences using the verb form indicated in parentheses:
a. She writes a report. (present continuous) b. They visited Paris last year. (present perfect) c. I will attend the conference. (future continuous) d. He solved the problem. (passive voice)
Identify the type of verb (action, linking, auxiliary, or modal) in each sentence:
a. The chef prepared a delicious meal. b. That sounds interesting. c. You should consider the proposal carefully. d. They have completed the project ahead of schedule.
🔍 Deep Dive
Verbs in English are incredibly versatile and can change form to express different meanings, times, and relationships. Understanding their nuances is essential for advanced English proficiency.
Verb Forms and Their Uses
Base Form (Infinitive):
The simplest form of a verb, used with "to" (to walk) or without "to" after modal verbs and in imperatives.
I want to travel around the world someday.
Please help me with this assignment.
Present Simple:
Used for habits, general truths, scheduled events, and narratives.
She works as a software engineer. (habit)
Water boils at 100°C at sea level. (general truth)
The train leaves at 8:30 tomorrow morning. (scheduled event)
In the final scene, the hero defeats the villain and saves the city. (narrative)
Past Simple:
Used for completed actions in the past.
I visited my grandparents last weekend.
Shakespeare wrote many famous plays.
Present/Past Continuous:
Used for actions in progress at a specific time.
They are developing a new application right now.
When I called, she was preparing dinner.
Present/Past Perfect:
Used for actions completed before another time or continuing to the present.
I have lived in this city for ten years. (continuing to present)
By the time I arrived, they had already left. (completed before another past action)
Future Forms:
Various ways to express future actions.
I will call you tomorrow. (simple future)
I'm going to buy a new car next month. (planned future)
The president is meeting with foreign diplomats next week. (scheduled future)
Transitive vs. Intransitive Verbs
Transitive Verbs
require a direct object to complete their meaning:
She wrote a novel. (novel = direct object)
They built a new house. (house = direct object)
Intransitive Verbs
do not require a direct object:
The baby slept peacefully.
She arrived late.
Some verbs can be both transitive and intransitive, with slightly different meanings:
He ran the company for 20 years. (transitive)
He runs every morning. (intransitive)
Regular vs. Irregular Verbs
Regular Verbs
follow predictable patterns when changing tense:
walk → walked → walked
play → played → played
Irregular Verbs
change form in unpredictable ways:
go → went → gone
see → saw → seen
bring → brought → brought
Phrasal Verbs
Combinations of verbs and particles (prepositions or adverbs) that create meanings different from the individual words:
break down (malfunction): My car broke down on the highway.
look up to (admire): Children often look up to their teachers.
put off (postpone): We had to put off the meeting until next week.
give up (surrender): Don't give up on your dreams.
Stative vs. Dynamic Verbs
Stative Verbs
describe states, feelings, or conditions rather than actions:
I believe in equal opportunities for all. (mental state)
She owns three houses. (possession)
This soup tastes delicious. (sensation)
Dynamic Verbs
describe actions or processes:
She's running a marathon this weekend.
They built a treehouse for their children.
I'm writing a research paper.
Stative verbs are typically not used in continuous forms:
Incorrect: I am knowing the answer. ❌
Correct: I know the answer. ✓
However, some verbs can be both stative and dynamic with different meanings:
I think she's right. (stative: opinion)
I'm thinking about my next career move. (dynamic: process of thought)
Mini Dialogues:
Situation: Job Interview
Interviewer: Could you tell me about a time when you had to overcome a significant challenge?
Candidate: In my previous role, I managed a project that was falling behind schedule. I reorganized the team structure and implemented daily check-ins, which helped us deliver on time.
Interviewer: That's impressive. How do you typically handle pressure in such situations?
Situation: Restaurant
Customer: Excuse me, I ordered the steak medium-rare, but this appears to be well-done.
Server: I apologize for the mistake. I'll take this back to the kitchen immediately and have the chef prepare a new one for you.
Customer: Thank you, I appreciate your quick response to the issue.
Situation: Academic Discussion
Professor: The research suggests that climate change has accelerated over the past decade.
Student: I've been reading about that. Have scientists determined the primary factors contributing to this acceleration?
Professor: They have identified several key factors, including increased industrial emissions and deforestation.
Common Errors and Formal Variations:
"I am having a car." ❌ → "I have a car." ✓ (stative verb misuse)
"She teached me French." ❌ → "She taught me French." ✓ (irregular verb form)
"I didn't went there." ❌ → "I didn't go there." ✓ (double past marking)
"They are wanting to expand their business." ❌ → "They want to expand their business." ✓ (stative verb in continuous)
"I will look into the matter." (formal) vs. "I'll check it out." (informal)
"The committee has reached a decision." (formal) vs. "They've decided." (informal)
"We shall proceed with the plan." (formal) vs. "We're going ahead with it." (informal)
📖 Reading Practice
The Evolution of a Career

When James first entered the corporate world fifteen years ago, he didn't anticipate how dramatically his career would transform over time. He began as an entry-level analyst, where he processed data and prepared reports for senior management. Although he performed well in this role, he soon realized that he wanted more responsibility.

After three years, he had developed sufficient expertise to apply for a promotion. The company recognized his potential and offered him a position managing a small team. James embraced this new challenge enthusiastically. He learned to delegate tasks effectively and mentored junior colleagues who looked up to him for guidance.

As technology evolved, so did James's skills. He has adapted to numerous software platforms and has implemented several innovative systems that streamlined operations. Currently, he is overseeing a major digital transformation project that will revolutionize how the company interacts with its clients.

"Throughout my career, I have encountered many obstacles," James reflects. "But I've discovered that each challenge presents an opportunity to grow. I am constantly learning and evolving, which keeps my work engaging and fulfilling."
Questions:
How has James's role changed since he first started working at the company?
What specific actions has James taken throughout his career development?
How does James view challenges in his professional life?
✏️ Practice Exercises
📘 Practice 1 - Sentence Correction
Identify and correct the verb errors in the following sentences:
She have been working on this project for months.
The team are planning to launch the product next week.
If I would have known about the problem, I would have fixed it.
They didn't meant to cause any trouble.
I am believing that education is the key to success.
He don't understand the instructions.
We was discussing the proposal when you called.
She has went to the conference last week.
📘 Practice 2 - Better Word Choice
Replace the basic verbs with more precise and sophisticated alternatives:
The company
made
a new policy regarding remote work. (Options: established, implemented, instituted, formulated)
The professor
said
that the assignment deadline had been extended. (Options: announced, declared, proclaimed, stated)
The storm
damaged
several buildings in the coastal area. (Options: devastated, ravaged, demolished, impaired)
The new evidence
showed
that the initial hypothesis was incorrect. (Options: demonstrated, revealed, indicated, substantiated)
The committee
looked at
all aspects of the proposal before making a decision. (Options: examined, scrutinized, evaluated, assessed)
The government
put off
the implementation of the new tax regulations. (Options: postponed, deferred, delayed, suspended)
📘 Practice 3 - Contextual Rewrites
Rewrite each sentence using the verb form specified in parentheses, maintaining the original meaning:
Scientists discover new species in the Amazon rainforest. (present perfect)
The company will announce the quarterly results next week. (future continuous)
She wrote an award-winning novel last year. (passive voice)
I visit my grandparents every Sunday. (present continuous for temporary arrangement)
They completed the project ahead of schedule. (past perfect)
The professor explains the concept clearly. (present perfect continuous)
The government implemented new policies. (passive voice, past perfect)
She speaks four languages fluently. (ability using modal verb)
📘 Practice 4 - Translation Challenge
Translate these Portuguese sentences into natural, idiomatic English, paying special attention to verb usage:
Eu estou trabalhando nesta empresa há cinco anos.
Se eu tivesse sabido da reunião, teria preparado uma apresentação.
Até o final do ano, teremos concluído o projeto.
Ela vem pensando em mudar de carreira ultimamente.
Quando cheguei em casa, ele já tinha saído.
Estou me formando em dezembro e pretendo fazer mestrado no exterior.
Você poderia me ajudar com estas traduções?
Venho notando uma melhora significativa no seu inglês.
🔁 Deep Review
Verbs are the engines of English sentences, driving meaning and determining how other elements function. Here's a summary of key points:
Verbs express actions, occurrences, or states of being
They change form to indicate time (tense), completion (aspect), who performs the action (voice), and attitude (mood)
Categories include action, linking, auxiliary, and modal verbs
Verbs can be transitive (requiring objects) or intransitive (not requiring objects)
Regular verbs follow predictable patterns; irregular verbs don't
Phrasal verbs combine verbs with particles to create new meanings
Stative verbs describe states and aren't typically used in continuous forms; dynamic verbs describe actions
Quick Review Questions:
What's the difference between transitive and intransitive verbs?
Why can't we usually use stative verbs in continuous forms?
How do phrasal verbs differ from regular verb + preposition combinations?
What determines whether to use present perfect or past simple when talking about past events?
🏠 Homework
📅 Day 1 - Writing

Write a personal narrative (200-250 words) about a significant change in your life. Use at least five different verb tenses and include at least three phrasal verbs. Underline each verb and identify its tense in parentheses afterward.
📅 Day 2 - Listening
Watch this TED Talk: "The Puzzle of Motivation" by Dan Pink (
https://www.ted.com/talks/dan_pink_the_puzzle_of_motivation
). Make notes of five interesting verb usages you notice (phrasal verbs, perfect tenses, modals, etc.). Write a brief summary (100 words) of the main points using some of these verb forms.
📅 Day 3 - Grammar
Rewrite these sentences, correcting any verb errors:
I am owning this house since 2010.
If I would have studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
She has went to the store yesterday.
They didn't meant to cause any trouble.
He don't understand the concept.
We was discussing the proposal when you called.
The team are planning to launch the product next week.
I have finish the report already.
📅 Day 4 - Speaking

Record yourself telling a story about a memorable experience. The recording should be 2-3 minutes long. Use at least three different verb tenses and include at least two phrasal verbs. After recording, listen to yourself and note any verb errors you made.
📅 Day 5 - Vocabulary/Context
Create a dialogue between two colleagues discussing a work project. The dialogue should be 12-15 exchanges long and include at least:
3 phrasal verbs
2 stative verbs
2 dynamic verbs
2 modal verbs
1 perfect continuous tense
1 future perfect tense
📅 Day 6 - Creativity/Reflection
Choose one option:
Write a short story (250-300 words) set in the future, using future tenses appropriately.
Write a reflection (250-300 words) on how your understanding of English verbs has evolved and how this knowledge has impacted your fluency and confidence in using the language.
